- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1-2 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending upward, model often lags; forecast 1-2 days ahead of true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been rising for 5+ days, model may overpredict; apply downward correction if sentiment is flat or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (last 7-10 days); add 0.5–1.0% buffer to end of forecast if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.00 entries, model is prone to “stuck” forecasts; introduce small upward drift (0.1–0.3) if price is trending up.
